title: Class-Based n-gram Models of Natural Language
authors: P. Brown, V. Della Pietra, P. deSouza, J. Lai, R. Mercer
before: n-gram models counted exact word sequences and assigned zero probability to anything unseen.
problem: Sparsity: most word sequences never appear in any corpus, however large.
breakthrough: Cluster words into classes automatically, so statistics are shared between similar words.
why: The first practical answer to sparsity by grouping words that behave alike, an idea embeddings later generalised.
next: Bengio's neural language model replaced discrete classes with continuous vectors.
inherits: The instinct that similar words should share statistical strength.
